analysis:
The change is documentation only (docs/architecture/inference.md): it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds notes that a serial-prefill Gemma 4 pipeline starts at its installed default lane width, with links to a 'Gemma pipeline lanes' anchor. The visible head text (lines 3048-3049, 3100-3101) matches the changed ranges. I examined the lane, owner-launch, cancellation, cache-tenant and add-on hold text in the visible excerpts.

No code, auth, attestation, encryption or wire behavior changes here. The prose is consistent with the existing threat model: prefix-cache tenant partitioning (T-041), the fixed typed owner launch with no peer-supplied environment or arguments, and live memory and request-capacity gates remaining per lane. The document says explicitly that multi-lane output equivalence and hardware qualification are not claimed, so it does not overclaim a security property.

Remaining questions are outside the supplied evidence. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the new 'Gemma pipeline lanes' section (head lines 4483-4538, 4901-4927) is not in the supplied units. Whether any source change enables a default of more than one Gemma 4 lane is therefore unverified. A later pass should check that the multi-lane default keeps the per-lane memory gate and prefix-cache salt scoping, and that a cancellation retiring a lane alone releases native state. Nothing in the supplied lines shows a regression. Because those sections and any accompanying source were not supplied, I flag deeper review as precautionary.
